subject: Re: MAP: Integration build plan (SDK, streaming, tool-calling, structured outputs) - owners & target close
messages:
From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme.com>

Cc: Tom Evans <tom.evans@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up + MAP draft request (integration milestones)

Thanks Marissa - great call today, appreciate the demo and the performance numbers.

Tom and I discussed next steps and we want to see a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with a clear integration build milestone that spells out: SDK integration owners, streaming support expectations, tool-calling surface (if applicable), structured outputs contract, and any dependencies that could block delivery. Can you share a draft MAP and a proposed target close date for this milestone?

We’re particularly concerned about:
- SDK compatibility with our stack (Node 18 + TypeScript)
- Real-time streaming latency and websocket support
- Security dependencies (SAML/KM integration; procurement/legal signoff)

Thanks - happy to jump back on a quick 20-min sync if you want to walk through the technical owners.

 - Sarah
Sarah Jones
Director of Product, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up + MAP draft request (integration milestones)

Hi Sarah - thanks for the clear asks and for taking the time today. Attached is a first-pass MAP draft (Acme_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf) focused on the Integration Build milestone. High level below; please see the PDF for a table view.

High-level MAP item (Integration Build Plan) - draft
- Target milestone name: Integration Build (SDK + Streaming + Tool-calling + Structured Outputs)
- Target milestone close date: 2026-03-20 (provisional)
- Success criteria: SDK integration completed with end-to-end sampling, streaming responses with <250ms token latency (p95) in staging, tool-calling flows validated, structured output schema accepted by Acme engineering.

Owners (internal / external)
- Redwood PM: Marissa Cole (overall MAP owner)
- Redwood SE: Dylan Brooks (integration technical lead, SDK + streaming)
- Redwood Eng: Dev Patel (examples, code samples, structured output templates)
- Acme Eng: Tom Evans (engineering owner)
- Acme Product: Sarah Jones (product acceptance)

Dependencies
- Procurement & legal signoff (DocuSign execution) - blocks access to Dedicated capacity if needed
- Access to staging environment and test datasets (Acme)
- Scoped list of tool-calling endpoints and expected input/output shapes (Acme + Redwood)

Next steps (proposed)
1) Dev to provide an integration build plan (owners, tasks, time estimates) - by 2026-02-28
2) Acme to provide sample dataset and tool-calling specs - by 2026-03-02
3) Joint staging test & validation - target window 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-15
4) Final acceptance & close milestone - target 2026-03-20

Attachments: Acme_MAP_Draft_v1.pdf (MAP table), acme_integration_samples.zip (code + examples stub)

I’m looping in Dylan and Dev to draft the owner-level integration plan and timing. Happy to set a 20-min sync if you prefer to walk through the plan.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Tom Evans <tom.evans@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP Integration Build Plan - owner-level technical plan

On Thu, Feb 26, 2026 at 09:30 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> High-level MAP item (Integration Build Plan) - draft
> - Target milestone name: Integration Build (SDK + Streaming + Tool-calling + Structured Outputs)

Hi all - putting together an owner-level build plan and technical notes below. A few assumptions: Acme is integrating via our Node/TS SDK, will use streaming websocket for low-latency tokens, and will optionally call external tools via our tool-calling interface.

Owner-level integration build plan (estimates)
- Week 0 (ASAP) - Kickoff and environment access
  - Owner: Marissa (Redwood) / Tom (Acme)
  - Tasks: Provide test credentials, staging hostnames, sample dataset
- Week 1 - SDK integration + basic request flow (2-3 dev days)
  - Owner: Dylan (Redwood SE) + Acme eng
  - Deliverable: Node example repo, auth flow (API key or mTLS depending on procurement), basic generation test
- Week 2 - Streaming integration + client validation (3-4 dev days)
  - Owner: Dylan (lead) / Dev (support)
  - Deliverable: Websocket streaming example with reconnection/resume logic, perf harness for p95 latency measurement
- Week 3 - Tool-calling integration & security review (4 dev days)
  - Owner: Dev (Redwood eng) + Acme eng
  - Deliverable: Tool schema, sample tool endpoints, security checklist (scoped access token exchange), end-to-end test
- Week 4 - Structured outputs & schema validation (2-3 dev days)
  - Owner: Dev (Redwood eng) + Acme product
  - Deliverable: JSON schema for structured outputs, sample validators, example test set
- Week 5 - Joint staging validation & acceptance (3 dev days)
  - Owner: Laura (CS) + Marissa (PM) + Acme product
  - Deliverable: Acceptance report, bug list, sign-off

Key technical notes / dependencies
- SDK: We will provide a Node 18+ TypeScript SDK example. If Acme needs client-side browser streaming, we’ll provide a small client sample that uses websocket endpoints and token refresh flow.
- Streaming: For <250ms token p95 we recommend using regional staging and continuous batching disabled for critical paths; Redwood can pin to a low-batch low-latency config for the Integration Build tests.
- Tool-calling: Need a canonical list of endpoints and input/output contracts from Acme. If tools make external HTTP calls, we’ll validate egress rules and secure token exchange patterns.
- Structured outputs: We’ll propose a draft JSON schema (Dev will attach sample validators) and allow Acme to propose changes.

Risks / blockers
- Legal/procurement delay for Dedicated capacity or enterprise contract - could push target close 2-3 weeks.
- Missing sample data or tool specs - blocks tool-calling and structured outputs validation.

I’ll upload the sample code bundle (acme_integration_samples.zip) to the shared link and push a small example repo to GitHub for Acme review by COB Mon 2/29.

 - Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
